title: Language Advantage Is a Function of the Executor: criteria self-audit and undecidability audit in cross-language code generation by LLM coders (timetable-ab)
description:
Current state (v1.7.6, 2026-11-02). This description states current values. Earlier revision notes remain in the version history; where an older note quotes a figure this one supersedes, this one governs.

The headline numbers. Language effect: inline JavaScript/Common Lisp = 1.008x (95% CI [0.829, 1.116]); abstraction = 1.007x ([0.879, 1.095]). Both intervals cross 1.0, so "identical" cannot be excluded. What survives is the writing style, not the language: collapsing repetition into one place saves 17% of characters (ratio 1.200x; as a saving interval 7.2%-30.7% in Common Lisp and 6.8%-26.6% in JavaScript, derived as 1 - 1/ratio from the ratio intervals [1.0771, 1.4423] and [1.0725, 1.3619] given in v4-ratios.tsv). Two earlier figures are withdrawn and named here rather than deleted: the "28-40% saving" (v1.6.0) and the "1.93x" language ratio quoted in older notes, which compared different abstraction levels, unequal JSON ecosystems and repeatedly registered runs.

What is re-checkable, and what is not. Two languages, a 15-operator specification, 36 invariants, plus 24 cells with archived prompts and frozen spec/criteria hashes. A second layer of 13 independent implementations under 80 invariants is kept as a prior account. Runs that did not archive their task descriptions are reported as observations, never as evidence.

Criteria self-audit (v1.7.0-v1.7.2). 88 criteria = 84 content + 2 form + 2 method (the numbers 81 and 82 are deliberately vacant, because H1/H2 live in a separate file), each newly added one proven able to fail by a counterexample. Three findings are recorded rather than hidden: the 36 scale criteria kill 0 of 12 mutants while the gate only ran the scale set; every assertion sits behind JSON.parse, so serialisation fidelity is constrained by nothing; and three mutants - leading whitespace, require("fs"), a JSON.parse call - are invisible to all 84 content criteria, caught only by H1/S1/S2 respectively. At v1.7.0, 8 of 84 content criteria had a counterexample; experiments/timetable-ab/counterexamples/ now ships a clean 84/84 base plus a mutation matrix that records, for each mutant, exactly which criteria turn red.

Undecidability is still the point. Established (3), refuted (3), undecidable (6). Missing conditions: C1 no weak-executor channel; C2 no exclusive machine or clock alignment; C3 a single model family. Incomplete rather than missing: C4 silent-failure coverage - 12 mutants audited, 8 killed, 4 survivors all classified, zero Class-A blind spots, which is not the same as "no blind spots"; C5 scale (at most 30 ops, at most 1k lines).

Protocol results. Expansion-time rejection (19/19 with validation off, load-time failure with it on); zero ceremony cost (0/0 manual edits); live-image REPL saves characters (9028 to 5957). S-expressions are not the most compact (CL 7506 vs JS 5933 characters at 5 ops); skill-pack intervention showed no main effect (0/6).

Gate and packaging (v1.7.5-v1.7.6). The regression gate now guards the v3-full criteria set by fingerprint, the frozen files by hash, and the release metadata itself: version must agree between CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json, the citation DOI must be the concept DOI, authors and contributors must agree on both sides, and both the notes and this description must mention the current version. Every added step was put through a destruction test - edited to break, observed to fail, restored, observed to pass - because a check that has never failed is not known to be a check. Still open: the counterexample step is not wired into the gate.

What this dataset does not do. It does not read "not detected" as "not present"; it does not extrapolate beyond the measured scale; it does not delete data - the timing columns, the retired line-count metric and all nineteen recorded failures of the measurement apparatus remain in the chronicle, annotated with their scope.

Included: run artefacts, frozen specifications with recorded sha256 freeze hashes, the 36 invariants with their go-red proofs, mutation scores with sample-size bounds, CONDITIONS.md, results.tsv with RESULTS-SCHEMA.md, an append-only chronicle (E-01 through E-05), CLAIMS.md, and the criteria-engineering documents (SPEC-AUDIT.md, CRITERIA-ENGINEERING.md, C4-REPORT.md, ATTACK-WEAK-COVERAGE.md, DO-NOT-MODIFY.md). Excluded: compiled binaries, build caches, machine-local temporary files, personal data.

Intended use: replication of the measurement protocol; reuse of the mutation-testing gate as a way to audit one's own criteria; and an empirical basis for benchmark-validity work in LLM code generation.
notes: v1.1.0 published 2026-10-30. v1.1.1 erratum. v1.4.0 two-layer split. v1.5.3 invariants 76 to 80. v1.6.0 criteria closure K1-K7, gate tamper tests, contract split, out-of-spec switch, add-n intervals, retraction of the 28-40% figure. v1.6.1 (2026-11-01) invariants #31/#32 written into the spec and the exclusion switch removed (CL first-pass 5/12 -> 2/12), package audit, correction banners on seven documents. v1.6.2 (2026-11-01) documentation only: headline figures replaced (1.93x -> 1.008x / 1.200x), withdrawn figure still named as withdrawn. v1.6.3 (2026-11-01) documentation only: confidence intervals annotated with resampling seed; bounds aligned to seed 20261101. v1.6.4 (2026-11-01) documentation only, PUBLICATION-ORDER CORRECTION. The v1.6.x line was uploaded out of order: v1.6.3 was published first (record 23858014) before v1.6.0-v1.6.2 had ever been published; those three were then rebuilt from their exact git commits (1.6.0=32e96c2, 1.6.1=7549717, 1.6.2=83da03e) and published afterwards, and v1.6.3 was republished last (23858146) so the concept DOI resolves to it. Zenodo record ids are monotonic, so the Versions list shows the true upload order 23858014 < 23858096 < 23858118 < 23858130 < 23858146 while the version numbers read 1.6.3, 1.6.0, 1.6.1, 1.6.2, 1.6.3. Every file state is genuine (git archive from the named commit; sha256 is that archive hash) and nothing was edited to fit the ordering; what is artificial is only the publication timestamps of v1.6.0-v1.6.2. Record 23858014 is a superseded duplicate and should be ignored in favour of 23858146. This release exists precisely because a reader comparing record ids would otherwise be right to suspect concealment. See docs/UPLOAD-ORDER.md in the package. v1.7.0 (2026-11-01) criteria engineering: three directions of auditing one's own criteria, and eight new criteria each proven able to fail. (1) SPEC-TO-CRITERIA direction: docs/SPEC-AUDIT.md walks every hard requirement in the frozen spec and names the check that covers it. 16 rows; uncovered rows went from 2 to 0. It has so far caught five behaviours that were correct in the implementations but completely unconstrained by any check. (2) CRITERIA-TO-IMPLEMENTATION direction: mutation audit over 12 mutants in runs/closure-mutants. 8 killed, 4 survived; every survivor classified (3 equivalent, 1 out-of-contract; 0 true blind spots). NOTE: check-scale.cjs killed 0 of 12 -- all 8 kills came from check-closure.cjs, and the regression gate only runs check-scale, so those 7 criteria are outside the gate's range. (3) CRITERIA-TO-CRITERIA direction: eight new criteria added, each with a counterexample proving it can go red: #83/#84 copyTo conflict, #85 n>=4, #86 copyTo duplicate name, H1 trailing AND leading whitespace (check-hygiene.cjs), H2 working-directory independence, S1 file IO, S2 JSON (check-static.cjs, source scanning). Strongest evidence: three counterexamples (leading whitespace, require("fs"), a JSON.parse call) leave check-v4 at its 78/84 baseline with byte-identical stdout -- invisible to all 84 content criteria, caught only by the new sets. H1 had its own defect when first written: /[ \t]$/ misses NBSP (U+00A0) entirely, and it only inspected line ends while check-v4's trim() eats line starts. Both fixed; now byte-level (0x20 / 0x09 / C2A0 / E38080). Total criteria: 84 (check-v4, numbering 1-80 and 83-86 -- 81/82 are vacant by design, living in check-hygiene as H1/H2) + 2 (hygiene) + 2 (static) = 88. check-closure K1-K7 belong to scale.spec and have zero discriminating power on v3-full (baseline is also 0/7); they must not be counted here. Blind replication: all 10 cells independently re-run by subagents, 10/10 identical to the candidate numbers (8 cells 78/84 with the same six camel-case failures, 2 cells 84/84). The 20 green results for H1/H2/S1/S2 are explicitly recorded as zero-information, not as achievement. Registered as an unreachable branch, not patched: swapDays conflict. Deleting the entire conflict check leaves output byte-identical across 7 adversarial input sets, because day-swapping preserves the no-overlap invariant, so a conflict cannot occur. Adding a criterion there would manufacture a false green. No existing number changed: character ratios, maintenance radius and all pass rates are untouched by this release. v1.7.1 (2026-11-01) documentation only: the blind-replication record for v1.7.0, plus a version map. docs/REPLICATION-v1.7-BASELINE.md has seven sections: the ten-cell baseline, the four hygiene/static criteria across ten cells, counterexample verification for all eight new criteria, a numbering-gap defect found during replication, execution notes, a second independent re-run, and one complete blind pass. That complete blind pass ran 20 keys through 54 checker invocations in a strict-parse mode that throws on any unparseable summary line, any inconsistency between the summary count and the per-case verdict lines, or any case-count mismatch. It finished with ALL PARSED OK after about 14.5 minutes. Its strongest result: three attack mutants are invisible to all 84 content criteria. Leading whitespace, require('fs'), and a JSON.parse call each leave check-v4 at exactly the source implementation's 78/84 with byte-identical stdout; they are caught only by H1, S1, and S2 respectively. The division of labour is recorded explicitly: check-v4 covers semantics, H1/H2 cover output form, S1/S2 cover implementation method, and none substitutes for another. A counting trap is recorded because it nearly produced a wrong conclusion: the attack baseline (tmp/attack-base.js) scores 84/84 while the ten cells score 78/84, because it is not the same code -- it implements the six table-level rewrite operators the cells lack. Attack mutants must therefore be compared within their own group, never subtracted from the ten-cell baseline. Stability: full-cl-macro run three times gives identical score, identical failing-criteria set and identical verdicts on all four hygiene/static criteria. docs/VERSION-MAP.md classifies every release from v1.5.0 to v1.7.0 as data / erratum / documentation, states what each changed, and explains v1.6.4 in particular: it is an instruction sheet for an upload-order accident, not a content update. Nothing in it describes the author's attempts, only what is observable. No data, criteria, or numbers changed in this release. v1.7.2 (2026-11-01) ERRATUM: one attribution in the v1.7.1 notes was wrong. v1.7.1 said the attack baseline scores 84/84 while the ten cells score 78/84 "because it is not the same code -- it implements the six table-level rewrite operators the cells lack". That explanation was wrong. The real cause is a single line. All six attack mutants dropped String(r.verb).toLowerCase() when derived, so every mutant carried six unrelated camel-case failures (#37 #38 #39 #42 #43 #49) on top of its intended change. attack-base.js kept that line and therefore scored 84/84; the ten cells do not have it and therefore score 78/84. The difference between them is that one line, nothing else. Decontaminated controls, restoring only that line and keeping each attack intact, give: copyto-noconflict 82/84 with only #83/#84 red; copyto-nodup 83/84 with only #86 red; n4 11/84 with 73 red including #85; and -- the important part -- leading whitespace, require("fs"), and a JSON.parse call each score 84/84 with NOTHING red. So the substantive claim gets stronger, not weaker: after decontamination those three mutations are invisible to all 84 content criteria; only H1, S1 and S2 catch them. The earlier "78/84, same as the source implementation" phrasing was contaminated arithmetic. Nature of this error: not a criterion error and not a data error, but an attribution error -- two numbers differed, and an explanation was invented without first listing which criteria actually differed. Had the six failures been listed first, they would have been visible as the same camel-case set as every other cell. Also recorded: check-v4.cjs was written to at 22:06:19 during replication (18727 to 19481 bytes, the extra 754 bytes being a header comment about the 81/82 numbering gap). Behaviour equivalence is pinned by two hard checks -- the old-version run A1 and the new-version runs S1-S3 produce byte-identical output, and A1-A4 re-run under the new version reproduce all twelve outputs byte for byte. The other three scripts and all ten implementations are unchanged by sha256. docs/REPLICATION-v1.7-BASELINE.md now carries a twelfth section recording this correction. No data, criteria, or measured number changed in this release. v1.7.3 (2026-11-01) documentation only: three gaps filled, one self-introduced numeric error corrected, and a new operating rule recorded. GAP 1-2: docs/RELEASE-NOTES-v1.7.1.md and docs/RELEASE-NOTES-v1.7.2.md did not exist. The blind-replication work and the attribution erratum lived only in these Zenodo notes, never as files in the package. Both are now shipped. GAP 3: README.md stopped at v1.6.1. Six releases were missing from its history section -- v1.6.2, v1.6.3, v1.6.4, v1.7.0, v1.7.1, v1.7.2. A reader landing on the README would have concluded the project had stopped. The section now runs to v1.7.2 and the README grew from 514 to 599 lines. CORRECTED, self-introduced: eighteen occurrences of the interval lower bound 0.825 were wrong. The authoritative table v4-ratios.tsv gives 0.8286 for the inline language ratio under seed=20261101, i.e. 0.829. v1.6.3 had already standardised this endpoint to 0.829 and the v1.7.0 documentation silently reverted it to the pre-seed value. All conclusion-bearing occurrences now read [0.829, 1.116]; the three places that legitimately describe the variation range (v4-ratios.tsv header, the v1.6.3 release notes, the README paragraph explaining seed dependence) keep 0.825-0.829 because there the number is the point. Also corrected: the correction letter quoted a saving interval of roughly 7-30%, which clips the JavaScript upper bound. The true 95% intervals are 7-29% for Common Lisp and 7-36% for JavaScript; the letter now states both. CONDITIONS.md carried two revoked figures as live conclusions: "symbolic layer valuable: established and quantified, saves 28-40%" and "language 0.97x". Both are now corrected to 17% (1.200x) and to 1.008x/1.007x with intervals, with the old values marked as withdrawn. CLAIMS.md gained three v1.7 rows: the three-direction audit (claim-43), the zero discriminating power of check-closure K1-K7 on v3-full (claim-44), and swapDays conflict as an unreachable branch (claim-45). BANNERS: eight historical documents that still present revoked figures as results (v3-report.md/.html, v3-report-complete.html, experiment-report.html, index.html, knock.md, paper-outline.md, experiments/timetable-ab/README.md) now carry a banner listing "what this text says" against "the current value". Their bodies are untouched -- they are the record of how the thinking went. NEW RULE, docs/DO-NOT-MODIFY.md: a batch script I wrote added that banner to tasks/v3-full.spec.md, whose sha256 is frozen in FREEZE-reproducible-layer-v3.1.txt. The hash changed from b202981a to c4b16f87, invalidating every freeze record for that spec. It was rolled back and the hash verified byte-identical. The rule recorded is that any script that writes files must carry a do-not-modify list that a machine can check, because remembering which files are frozen does not work. CONTAMINATION CHECK before this release: the frozen spec hash is unchanged; all 728 files under runs/ carry last-modified times no later than 16:59, so no experiment artefact was touched tonight; the three checker scripts were modified at 21:34-22:06 as part of the criteria work and are accounted for in SPEC-AUDIT and the v1.7.0 notes. No data, criteria, or measured number changed in this release. Every change is to how the numbers are described or where they are documented. v1.7.4 (2026-11-02) ERRATUM to v1.7.3. The saving interval was wrong in two places. v1.7.3 stated the 95% intervals as 7-29% (Common Lisp) and 7-36% (JavaScript). Both upper bounds were wrong, and they were wrong because they had been copied from a table rather than derived. The authoritative ratio intervals are [1.0771, 1.4423] for CL and [1.0725, 1.3619] for JS; converting a ratio interval into a saving interval requires 1 - 1/ratio, which gives 7.2%-30.7% for CL and 6.8%-26.6% for JS. The older v1.6.3 release notes had already recorded exactly these figures and explicitly warned that 7-29% was an estimate; v1.7.3 regressed by quoting that estimate back, and added a second error by putting 36% on the JavaScript side. Corrected in docs/B1-加n结果.md with the derivation shown inline, so the next reader does not have to trust the endpoint. No measurement, criterion or dataset changed - only the arithmetic connecting a ratio interval to a saving interval. Note for the record: the correction letter itself is not part of this package, so the wrong interval never left this archive; the earlier statement that "the letter now states both" was true of a draft that has since been corrected again. v1.7.5 (2026-11-02): the regression gate now guards the v3-full criteria set and the frozen files, and the project chronicle records both days of criteria work. GAP FOUND: gate.cjs had four steps, all built around scale.spec (30 ops, 36 criteria, K1-K7). It did not know that check-v4.cjs, check-hygiene.cjs or check-static.cjs existed. Delete either of the latter two and the gate stayed green. Rewrite any criterion inside check-v4.cjs so it always passes and the gate stayed green. Alter tasks/v3-full.spec.md by one byte, invalidating every freeze record, and the gate stayed green. docs/DO-NOT-MODIFY.md had stated the rule that any file-writing script must carry a machine-checkable do-not-modify list, but no code enforced it. STEP 5 ADDED: fingerprints for the three v3-full criteria files, recorded in a new v3-baseline.json alongside the ten-cell baseline floors (eight cells at 78/84, two at 84/84). The floors run only under --v3-baseline because six of the ten cells are Common Lisp and take 65-77 seconds each, roughly twelve minutes in total. STEP 6 ADDED: the three frozen files are hashed and compared against a new frozen-files.json. That file is not written by hand -- make-frozen-list.cjs derives it from the FREEZE-*.txt records, so the list and the records cannot drift apart. Where a file was amended, the current hash wins and the superseded one is kept with a note. BOTH STEPS WERE PUT THROUGH DESTRUCTION TESTS, because a check that has never failed is not known to be a check. Step 5: editing check-static.cjs produced "1 mismatch, FAIL, naming check-static.cjs"; the file was restored and the hash verified byte-identical, then the gate returned to green. Step 6: appending a single space to tasks/v3-full.spec.md produced "1 mismatch, FAIL, naming tasks/v3-full.spec.md (now 1f5ce6e2, recorded b202981a)"; restored, hash verified back to b202981ae0ae5659, gate green again. CHRONICLE: docs/experiment-report.md gained Erratum E-04 (v1.1.0 through v1.7.4: the three audit directions, the 88-criteria count with its 84+2+2 decomposition and the deliberately vacant 81 and 82, the three hardest findings, the eight registered criteria errors classified A/B/C, and the two numeric errors introduced by the author) plus an addendum covering this morning gate work. E-01 through E-03 are untouched; the chronicle remains append-only and now runs to 2678 lines. STILL OPEN, recorded rather than quietly omitted: the counterexample step is not done. Three mutants -- leading whitespace, require(fs), a JSON.parse call -- are invisible to all 84 content criteria, but they live in tmp/ and not in the package, so the gate cannot automatically verify that the criteria are still able to fail. That is the next hole. CONSISTENCY FIX: CITATION.cff had been left at 1.7.3 while .zenodo.json said 1.7.4; both now read 1.7.5. CONTAMINATION SWEEP before release: frozen spec hash unchanged, all 728 artefacts under runs/ untouched since 16:59 on 11-01, every quoted interval endpoint matching the authoritative v4-ratios.tsv, and no residual copies of the two wrong saving bounds except in passages that describe them as historical errors. No measurement, criterion or dataset changed. This release adds enforcement, not evidence.v1.7.6 (2026-11-02): the contributor record had never been updated, and the public description had stopped at v1.6.3. BOTH ARE FIXED. THE CONTRIBUTOR GAP: CITATION.cff put the assistant into the authors list with two fields that the CFF 1.2.0 schema does not allow there (type, contribution - additionalProperties is false on definitions.person), and carried no contributors section at all; .zenodo.json had the contributor but with no description of what was contributed, and that entry had not changed since the first commit. The citation now has a real contributors section whose text covers the criteria engineering, the blind-replication driver, gate steps 5-7 and the record of self-correction, and both files name the same two parties. THE DESCRIPTION GAP, which is the more serious of the two: the record description - the text a reader sees first, byte-identical to what was published for v1.7.5 - still opened with v1.6.3 and stated nothing about v1.7.0 through v1.7.5. It also carried three withdrawn values as live results: the interval lower bound 0.825 (corrected to 0.829 in v1.7.3, 18 occurrences), "1.93x" as refuted evidence (withdrawn in v1.6.0), and "nine surviving mutants" (superseded by the C4 audit: 12 mutants, 8 killed, 4 survivors classified, zero Class-A blind spots). Two further counts were stale: a chronicle whose stated line count had stopped matching the file and 14 frozen specifications (5 FREEZE records). The description is rewritten to state current values; the withdrawn figures are named as withdrawn rather than removed. THE CITATION DOI, third time: v1.7.5 notes claimed "both now read 1.7.5" while CITATION.cff still pointed at 10.5281/zenodo.23871162, the v1.7.4 record. The version had been changed and the DOI had not. It is now the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23618044, so that it cannot fall behind a release again. STEP 7 ADDED to the gate, and this is why the failure can be caught mechanically: version equality between CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json; citation DOI must be the concept DOI; authors must equal creators and contributors must equal contributors on both sides; and both notes and description must mention the current version. This step fails on the v1.7.5 state and passes on the current one; both directions were observed. STEP 7 WAS REWRITTEN THREE TIMES, AND EACH ROUND WAS CAUGHT BY A BLIND SUBAGENT. V1: String.includes on the description. A subagent changed one occurrence of v1.7.6 to v1.7.60 and the check still passed - the most ordinary typo there is. V2: bounded regular expression. The first attempt forbade dots in the lookbehind as well as digits, so the notes sentence "...not evidence.v1.7.6 (2026-11-02)" - where the version follows a full stop - was judged as missing the version, and three tests went red on the same sentence. Red for the wrong reason is a fake test. Fixed to forbid digits only; four tests then passed. A second round then found two more greens: changing ONLY the first occurrence to v1.7.60 passed (the criterion asked "mentioned somewhere", not "the first sentence is right"), and setting version to 1.7 on both sides passed (the version was pasted into the regex as a literal, and v1.7 is followed by a dot, so the right boundary held). V3: no regular expression at all. Three parts: the version must match ^(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$, rejecting leading zeros; every vX.Y[.Z] in notes and description is extracted and the current version must be exactly in that list; and the FIRST version number in the description must equal the current version, because the first sentence is the one a reader sees. SIX TESTS: full replacement fails; only-the-first-occurrence fails on "first version is v1.7.60"; version=1.7 fails on "not three-part"; reordering authors passes; one extra author fails; restore passes with byte-identical hashes. KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED, stated in the code comment rather than left implicit: v1.7.6.1 and v1.7.6x are extracted as "1.7.6", and extraction runs over raw text so an HTML attribute value also counts as an occurrence. These require deliberate construction, and what this criterion protects against is forgetting to bump the version - which is what actually happened in v1.7.5 - not an adversary. Adding criteria for inputs that cannot occur naturally is the same error as manufacturing green. A test-design error is recorded too: the first attempt at the full-replacement test changed only one of the two occurrences and therefore passed; that was the test not being thorough, not the criterion being blind.  CORRECTED IN PASSING: CLAIMS.md claim-31 still stated the saving interval as "[7%, 29-36%]", mixing the two languages and using the two upper bounds that v1.7.4 had identified as wrong; it now gives 7.2%-30.7% (CL) and 6.8%-26.6% (JS) with the derivation. README.md still pointed new readers at tools/gate.cjs, which is the early general-purpose gate and does not contain steps 5-7; the pointer now names experiments/timetable-ab/gate.cjs and says what the difference is. MEASURED THIS RELEASE, not prose: the ten-cell baseline was re-run end to end and the raw stdout kept under experiments/timetable-ab/baseline-v17/ - 10 cells, 255.1 s total, 8 cells at 78/84 and 2 at 84/84, every score at or above the recorded floor, and the six red criteria identical in every cell (#37 #38 #39 #42 #43 #49, the camel-case verb line). The recorded cost of "65-77 seconds per Common Lisp cell, roughly twelve minutes" was wrong: the actual range is 25.0-37.7 s per Lisp cell and 8.1-8.2 s per JavaScript cell. ALSO MEASURED: a clean 84/84 base (counterexamples/base-clean.js) was reconstructed, and a mutation matrix was run over it, so that each mutant now ships with the exact set of criteria it turns red. The point is not to produce red output but to answer a countable question: for how many of the 84 content criteria does an implementation exist that makes that criterion fail? STILL OPEN, recorded: the counterexample matrix is not yet wired into the gate as a step; 12 releases from v1.1.0 to v1.6.4 have no RELEASE-NOTES file; and git HEAD still sits at the v1.6.3 commit, so the "rebuilt from the named git commit" chain does not cover v1.7.x. No measurement, criterion or dataset value changed in this release.
